host_steps.note: BSP_GameSettings_GetSingleton. Eleven call sites in the prologue, 00932A22 through 00932B64. The reconstruction takes the physics material record as a ShipHydroInputs field instead of a host method, because the settings singleton is another packet's address.

Indirect: MOV EAX,[EDX+5Ch] then CALL EAX with the argument 8. The same slot is called again at 00932E2F inside the element loop. The callee's body was not read, so the method is named by the record it selects, not by a recovered meaning.

The call whose returned pointer the MOVSS at 00932A96 indexes as settings+4E0h+material*38h. The seven coefficient reads are 00932A96, 00932AAD, 00932AC4, 00932ADB, 00932AF2, 00932B09 and 00932B20, each preceded by its own CALL 00424C40; the eighth read, at 00932B3F, is the Kitevo exponent at +50Ch.
The body's linear velocity, M+00h. Returns a pointer the caller copies into three floats.
The body's angular velocity, M+0Ch.
LEA EAX,[ECX+8]; RET. Returns body+8h, the 3x4 world transform, which the next call expands.
Dyn_Transform_Expand3x4To4x4. Rows 0..2 become the body axes and row 3 the position; out+0Ch/+1Ch/+2Ch take 0.0f and out+3Ch the 1.0f at 00D7A24C.
The CRT invalid-argument handler, reached when the element list is empty. Not modelled: the reconstruction's loop simply does not run for a zero count.
BSP_Vector3f_TransformAffinePoint on the element's local point at element+18h, giving the world point the water height is sampled under.
The same point with its local Y forced to zero (the XORPS at 00932CEE into the middle slot at 00932CF9). The world result less the transform's translation is the lever arm every torque uses.
BSP_GameWorld_SampleWaterHeight on the world at [00E188A8]+19F0h, arguments (world x, world z). The FSUBR at 00932D70 turns it into the element's height above water.
BSP_Vector3f_Cross with a = the angular velocity and b = the lever arm, so the result is omega x r and the element's point velocity is the linear velocity plus it.
The second site, per element. A non-zero answer makes the buoyancy shape mix 0.0f instead of the 0.5f at 00CE3800.
The CRT square root on the squared point speed. Called again at 0093300B for the Kitevo == 0.5 branch of the exponent ladder.

BSP_Geometry_NormalizeVectorWithFloor in place on the copy of the point velocity at ESP+78h. Every drag projection is taken against the normalised vector, the magnitude coming from the separate speed and speed-squared terms.
The planing cross product, (magnitude * row1) x (Length * 0.5 * row2), subtracted from the torque accumulator at 00933918.
The element's own torque, lever arm crossed with the element force, added to controller+384h.
BSP_LeakManager_Update on unit+10D4h with the same dt. Already reconstructed in include/bsp/unit_forces.hpp; reused as a contract.
The leak model's heeling torque, staged into controller+74h..+7Ch and added to the torque accumulator at 00933AA7. Already reconstructed in include/bsp/unit_forces.hpp.
Dyn_Body_AddForce with controller+378h..+380h. The only AddForce call site in the image.
Dyn_Body_AddTorque with controller+384h..+38Ch.
DISABLED PATH ONLY. Reached when controller+14h is non-zero (CMP at 009329C9, JZ to the live path at 00932A1F). Zeroes the linear velocity.
The same path, zeroing the angular velocity. 00932A16 then ORs bit 2 into body+50h and 00932A1A jumps straight to the accumulator zeroing at 00933B40.

corrections.was: It is the only code on a live hull's path that writes the body's linear velocity outside 0092D300: 009329EC calls 00C37E50 (set linear velocity) and 00932A0E calls 00C37E20 (set angular velocity).
corrections.is: Both calls are on the DISABLED path. 009329C9 compares controller+14h with zero and jumps to the live path at 00932A1F when it is clear; 009329CF..00932A1A is the other branch, which zeroes both velocities, ORs bit 2 into body+50h and jumps to the accumulator zeroing. The live path never writes a velocity: it writes force and torque through 00C35360 and 00C35330.
corrections.evidence: 009329c9 CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x14],0x0 / 009329cd JZ 0x00932a1f / 00932a1a JMP 0x00933b40. docs/UNIT_FORCE_CHANNEL.md lines 42 and 43 already had this right.

corrections.was: eight floats out of settings + 4E0h + material*38h at 00932A96, 00932AAD, 00932AC4, 00932ADB, 00932AF2, 00932B09, 00932B20 and 00932B3F ... the six record fields ... the readers of KozegellenallasiEgyutthato*
corrections.is: Seven drag coefficients are read, at +4E0h through +4F8h; the eighth address in that list, 00932B3F, reads Kitevo at +50Ch. KozegellenallasiEgyutthatoNElore at +4FCh is never read by 009329C0, which is why the forward drag term at 0093324E is linear only. The CALL 00424C40 at 00932B32 discards its result, which is where the eighth coefficient read would have been. The record has fourteen fields, not six.
corrections.evidence: 00932a96..00932b20 are the seven MOVSS reads; 00932b32 CALL 0x00424c40 with no use of EAX; 00932b3f MOVSS XMM0,[EAX + EDI*0x1 + 0x50c]; 0093324e FLD [ESP+0x1c] / 00933252 FMUL [ESP+0x1b4] / 00933259 FMUL ST1 with no speed-squared term.

corrections.target: docs/UNIT_RUDDER_CURVE.md, Corrections, the settings row at +4E0h
corrections.was: This mapping is inferred from the key names and the row stride, not from a read of the loader's stores into that range.
corrections.is: Confirmed, not corrected. The loader's own stores bind every offset to its key: 0083FFE2 stores +4E0h for the key pushed at 0083FFAA (00D0A764 KozegellenallasiEgyutthatoL) and the pattern continues to 008403B7 / +514h (Friction). The published order is right in every position.

corrections.target: docs/UNIT_RUDDER_CURVE.md, Corrections: 'The doc's note that variant 1 forces +50Ch to 2.0f conflicts with the shipped TBoat value of 0.5; a re-read of the branch around 00932B00 should settle which.'
corrections.is: Settled: both are true and the override wins. 00932B3C compares the material index with 1 and 00932B53 overwrites the loaded exponent with the 2.0f at 00CE3958. The shipped TBoat Kitevo of 0.5 is therefore dead for this routine, though 00937C90's displacement sum reads +50Ch without the override and does use it.

corrections.target: docs/UNIT_RUDDER_CURVE.md, Corrections: 'Gravitacio = 10.0 the source of the 10.0 double at 00CE3DC0'
corrections.was: the record's Gravitacio is the source of the 10.0 in 009329C0
corrections.is: Not in 009329C0. The multiply at 0093303E is FMUL double ptr [0x00CE3DC0], a literal 10.0, and the buoyancy weight at 00933A41 is the same literal. The record's +30h Gravitacio is read by 00937C90's displacement sum, where it appears as Gravitacio divided by that same literal 10.0. The value 10.0 matches the world gravity magnitude at 00CE6848, which is why the buoyancy cancels it.
corrections.evidence: 0093303e FMUL double ptr [0x00ce3dc0] and 00933a41 FMUL double ptr [0x00ce3dc0]; no read of +510h anywhere in 009329C0.

corrections.target: the packet brief, 'the yaw/roll/pitch damping torques'
corrections.was: the routine has separate angular damping terms
corrections.is: It has none. Every torque in the routine is a lever-arm cross product of a linear force: the element's own r x F at 009339A7, the planing term at 009338F6 and the leak model's heeling torque at 00933A52. Angular damping is the rigid body's own M+BCh rate, which 00939A2F sets to 1.0f. What damps a turn is the lateral drag acting at each element's offset from the body origin, which is a yaw torque by geometry rather than by a coefficient.
corrections.evidence: the three 004F9B30 / 0074F2E0 sites are the only writers of controller+384h..+38Ch in the body.

probe.body: B, the class-built hull body (DeRuyter, mass 7688)
notes: The buoyancy total of 76880.0 is exactly mass * 10, the world gravity magnitude, so the hull neither sinks nor rises. That is the stand-in element list being solved for neutral buoyancy, not a recovered number.
The final distance is larger than the minimum because the ship AI has no stop: it reaches the goal and circles it. The minimum distance is the convergence measure.

The 3.0e6 yaw torque does nothing in this run: the probe attaches no collision shape, so the AABB span is zero, 00C37E70 stores a zero inverse inertia and no torque moves the hull. With a real span this term would be the turn damping.
Body A in the same run is the hand-built stand-in with a zero inverse mass, so the force cannot move it; its 87.5 degree drift is the no-body control, unchanged by --hydro.
